<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/5834):

>## Summary
>
>On fencing-induced reboots in Two-Node with Fencing (DualReplica) clusters, a boot-ordering race between `corosync.service` and `ovs-configuration.service` causes a reboot loop:
>
>1. Both services start after `NetworkManager-wait-online.service` (which fails because `br-ex` doesn't exist yet on reboot)
>2. Corosync starts in <1s and binds to `enp2s0` (standalone NIC with the corosync address)
>3. ~19s later, `configure-ovs.sh` creates `br-ex` and migrates `enp2s0` to an OVS port — stripping the address corosync is bound to
>4. knet detects link down within 84ms, the 3000ms TOTEM token timeout fires, and the surviving node re-fences via Redfish
>5. The rebooted node enters a fencing loop (observed: 8 reboots in 9 minutes in CI)
>
>This PR adds a systemd drop-in for `corosync.service` on TNF clusters that orders it `After=ovs-configuration.service`, ensuring the OVS bridge is fully configured before corosync starts. This is a passive ordering constraint — it has no effect on clusters without `ovs-configuration.service`.
>
>**Impact**: Both IPv6 and IPv4 TNF CI jobs are affected. IPv6 sees full reboot loops (73% failure rate). IPv4 avoids the loop due to faster DHCP but still experiences TOTEM timeouts disrupting pacemaker state (93% failure rate on shard 1of3).
>
>## Root cause timeline (Boot 2, Run `2038453784169943040`, IPv6)
>
>| Time | Event |
>|------|-------|
>| 06:11:15.589 | `corosync.service` starts — binds to `enp2s0` |
>| 06:11:34.861 | `configure-ovs.sh` starts |
>| 06:11:37.338 | `br-ex` created, `enp2s0` moved to OVS port |
>| 06:11:38.505 | knet: link DOWN (84ms after interface state change) |
>| 06:11:39.897 | TOTEM: token timed out (3000ms) |
>| 06:11:40.008 | DHCPv6 assigns address to `br-ex` — too late |
>| 06:11:43.499 | Node fenced again → reboot loop |
>
>## Expected behavior after fix
>
>```
>06:11:15  NetworkManager-wait-online fails
>06:11:15  ovs-configuration starts
>06:11:34  configure-ovs.sh creates br-ex, migrates enp2s0 to OVS port
>06:11:44  ovs-configuration finishes → corosync can now start
>06:11:44  Corosync starts, binds to br-ex (already configured) — no race
>```
>
>~30s delay in corosync start on fencing reboots. Negligible against the 1200s test timeout.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [ ] Verify `corosync.service` drop-in is rendered only for `DualReplica` topology (TNF clusters)
>- [ ] Verify `corosync.service` starts after `ovs-configuration.service` on fencing reboot
>- [ ] Verify no impact on non-TNF clusters (drop-in only delivered to `two-node-with-fencing` MachineConfig)
>- [ ] IPv6 TNF CI job passes without reboot loops
>- [ ] IPv4 TNF CI job passes without TOTEM timeout disruption
>
>/jira [OCPEDGE-2447](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPEDGE-2447)
>
>🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code)

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/5834):

>## Summary
>
>On fencing-induced reboots in Two-Node with Fencing (DualReplica) clusters, a boot-ordering race between `corosync.service` and `ovs-configuration.service` causes a reboot loop:
>
>1. Both services start after `NetworkManager-wait-online.service` (which fails because `br-ex` doesn't exist yet on reboot)
>2. Corosync starts in <1s and binds to `enp2s0` (standalone NIC with the corosync address)
>3. ~19s later, `configure-ovs.sh` creates `br-ex` and migrates `enp2s0` to an OVS port — stripping the address corosync is bound to
>4. knet detects link down within 84ms, the 3000ms TOTEM token timeout fires, and the surviving node re-fences via Redfish
>5. The rebooted node enters a fencing loop (observed: 8 reboots in 9 minutes in CI)
>
>**Impact**: Both IPv6 and IPv4 TNF CI jobs are affected. IPv6 sees full reboot loops. IPv4 avoids the loop due to faster DHCP but still experiences TOTEM timeouts disrupting pacemaker state.
>
>## Changes
>
>This PR delivers two systemd drop-ins, scoped to TNF clusters only (`two-node-with-fencing` MachineConfig):
>
>### 1. Corosync boot-ordering drop-in (`corosync.service.d/10-after-ovs-configuration.conf`)
>
>Adds `Wants=ovs-configuration.service` and `After=ovs-configuration.service` to `corosync.service`. Both directives are required:
>
>- **`After=`** orders corosync after ovs-configuration, but only if both are in the same systemd start transaction
>- **`Wants=`** pulls ovs-configuration into corosync's start transaction — without it, `After=` is silently ignored because the two units are in different activation chains (`multi-user.target` vs `kubelet-dependencies.target`)
>
>`Wants=` is a weak dependency: if `ovs-configuration.service` fails, corosync still starts. On non-TNF clusters, the drop-in is not delivered.
>
>### 2. OVS re-execution guard (`ovs-configuration.service.d/10-skip-rerun.conf`)
>
>Adds `ConditionPathExists=!/var/run/ovs-config-executed` to `ovs-configuration.service`. This prevents `configure-ovs.sh` from re-running within the same boot when `Wants=` triggers it from corosync's late start (~22 minutes after initial boot, during CEO handover).
>
>Without this guard, the second run of `configure-ovs.sh` clears `ovn-remote` (line 13 of the script, unconditional), breaking OVN pod networking during installation. The marker file (`/var/run/ovs-config-executed`) is created by `configure-ovs.sh` on line 22 of every successful run. Since `/var/run` is tmpfs, the marker resets on reboot — allowing normal execution on fencing-induced reboots while preventing re-execution within the same boot.
>
>**Note**: The drop-in YAML file is intentionally named `ovs-configuration-skip-rerun.service.yaml` (not `ovs-configuration.service.yaml`) to avoid a filename collision with the base unit template in `common/_base/units/`. MCO's template renderer keys by filename with last-write-wins semantics — using the same filename would replace the base unit definition entirely, losing `ExecStart` and all service configuration.
>
>## Why `After=` alone doesn't work
>
>The first version of this PR had only `After=ovs-configuration.service`. CI validation (5 runs) showed the same failure — corosync started 20-28s before ovs-configuration on every fencing reboot.
>
>Debugged on a live two-node cluster:
>- Drop-in file present on disk at `/etc/systemd/system/corosync.service.d/`
>- `systemctl show corosync.service` confirmed `After=...ovs-configuration.service` in resolved deps
>- **But** `systemctl list-dependencies corosync.service` showed ovs-configuration was NOT in the dependency tree
>
>`After=` is an ordering constraint, not a requirement. It means "if both are starting, start me second" — but if the other unit isn't enqueued, it has no effect. Adding `Wants=` fixes this.
>
>## Live test results
>
>After applying `Wants=` + `After=` on a local cluster and rebooting:
>
>```
>Apr 07 13:29:00  Starting Configures OVS...              (ovs-configuration starts)
>Apr 07 13:29:03  ovs-configuration.service: Deactivated   (ovs-configuration finishes)
>Apr 07 13:29:03  Starting Corosync Cluster Engine...      (corosync starts AFTER)
>Apr 07 13:29:04  Started Corosync Cluster Engine
>```
>
>No knet link-down, no TOTEM timeout, no fencing.
>
>## Root cause timeline (Boot 2, Run `2038453784169943040`, IPv6)
>
>| Time | Event |
>|------|-------|
>| 06:11:15.589 | `corosync.service` starts — binds to `enp2s0` |
>| 06:11:34.861 | `configure-ovs.sh` starts |
>| 06:11:37.338 | `br-ex` created, `enp2s0` moved to OVS port |
>| 06:11:38.505 | knet: link DOWN (84ms after interface state change) |
>| 06:11:39.897 | TOTEM: token timed out (3000ms) |
>| 06:11:40.008 | DHCPv6 assigns address to `br-ex` — too late |
>| 06:11:43.499 | Node fenced again → reboot loop |
>
>## CI validation
>
>- Apr 7-8 (Wants=+After= only, no ConditionPathExists): **3/4 PASSED** (1 unrelated failure — member not removed after graceful shutdown). Reboot loop eliminated.
>- Apr 13 (+ ConditionPathExists guard): awaiting results
>
